name: p4-0410-verbosity-zoom
title: Verbosity flags as zoom levels
spec: 1600-wide SVG, six stacked rows from none to -vvvvv, each adding detail. none: task names, results, recap. -v: module return data (rc, stdout, stderr). -vv: task paths, false_condition for skipped tasks, file loading. -vvv: SSH command lines, remote temp paths, module args. -vvvv: connection plugin internals, very noisy. -vvvvv: everything including WinRM and SSH raw debugging. Side note: most problems are visible at -vvv. Orange on the -vvv row only.
alt: Six rows showing what each verbosity level adds to the output, from none to five v flags.
cap: Start at the default level and add one v at a time, because most problems are visible at three v.

name: p4-0410-four-questions-case
title: Four questions on a three-of-200 failure
spec: 1600-wide SVG, four question boxes in order with the worked answers. When did it fail: at a task, not parsing, so the parse drawer is closed. Where did it fail: three of the 200 nodes, so the cause is something those three have. What changed: those three were re-imaged last week. Can you reproduce it: --limit on one of them with -vvv shows a missing package. Result box: privilege or module layer, machine state was wrong and the playbook was not. Orange on the result box.
alt: Four questions applied to a driver task failing on three of 200 nodes, ending at a missing package in the module layer.
cap: Comparing a failing host with a passing one points to machine state rather than the playbook.

name: p4-0410-investigation-flags
title: Investigation commands from cheapest to most targeted
spec: 1600-wide SVG vertical ladder of commands from cheapest: --syntax-check (parse only, touches no host), --list-tasks --list-tags --list-hosts, --check --diff --limit gpu001 (what would change), --step (confirm every task y/n/c), --start-at-task Install driver, -t config -l gpu001, ad hoc setup with filter=ansible_default_ipv4, ad hoc command which python3 with -vvv. Warning box beside --start-at-task: it skips earlier set_fact so the driver task fails on an undefined variable. Orange on the warning box.
alt: A ladder of Ansible investigation commands with a warning that start-at-task skips earlier set_fact tasks.
cap: Start-at-task skips the earlier tasks, so a variable they set may be undefined and cause a misleading error.

name: p4-0410-ssh-step-chain
title: Four steps to an SSH session and the failure at each
spec: 1600-wide SVG chain of four steps left to right with the failing message under each. Name resolves to an address: Could not resolve hostname, fix with ansible_host or DNS. Packet reaches the port: Connection timed out or No route to host, check nc -vz host 22. Server accepts the handshake: Host key verification failed or kex_exchange_identification, check known_hosts and MaxStartups. Login succeeds: Permission denied (publickey,password), check ssh -vvv, ansible_user, ssh-add -l. Note: a failure at one step makes every later step impossible. Orange on the first failing-step note.
alt: A four-step chain from name resolution to login with the typical error message at each step.
cap: A login error tells you nothing if the network step before it is still failing.

name: p4-0410-ssh-key-hygiene
title: Host key change and automation key hardening
spec: 1600-wide SVG two panels. Left: a re-imaged node changes its Ed25519 host key, OpenSSH aborts with Host key verification failed and WARNING REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED, confirm the rebuild was expected, then ssh-keygen -R 192.168.33.10 and ssh-keyscan -H 192.168.33.10 appended to known_hosts. Right: sshd_config PasswordAuthentication no and PermitRootLogin no, ansible.posix.authorized_key with key_options no-port-forwarding and from the control node IP, exclusive true removes unauthorized keys so a departed admin's key stops working. Orange on exclusive true.
alt: Two panels, one on replacing a changed host key and one on hardening the automation SSH key.
cap: Replace a host key only after confirming the rebuild, and use exclusive true so old keys are removed.

name: p4-0410-which-value-wins
title: Checking which variable value is used
spec: 1600-wide SVG checklist flow for a wrong value. Box 1 which value is used: ansible-inventory --host, debug var, -vvv, grep; extra vars with -e sit at the top of the stack and role vars/ also beats inventory. Box 2 type: var | type_debug shows str, int, bool, list, dict. Box 3 render template: ansible localhost -m template with -e @vars.yml, inspect /tmp/out. Box 4 condition: debug msg of the when expression, -vv false_condition. Example strip: gpu_count 8 from -e is a number, from a CSV it is the text 8 and the when comparison fails. Orange on the example strip.
alt: A checklist for finding which variable value wins and what type it has, with a CSV text-versus-number example.
cap: A value that arrives as text instead of a number breaks a comparison even though the code did not change.

name: p4-0410-slow-run-causes
title: Slow playbook causes and levers
spec: 1600-wide SVG, measure-first flow. Top box: profile_tasks and timer callbacks, write down the run time, change one setting, measure again, undo if it did not move. Below, six cause to fix rows: fact gathering slow (subset or cache, gathering smart, fact_caching jsonfile); apt update every run (cache_valid_time); per-item loops or git clone on every host (single calls); serial 1 on a huge group or forks 5 (forks); SSH setup slow (ControlPersist, pipelining, sshd reverse DNS); strategy linear waits for stragglers (strategy free for independent work). Footer: very large fleets use ansible-pull, AWX or AAP execution nodes. Orange on the measure-first box.
alt: A measure-first box above six common causes of a slow playbook and the setting that addresses each.
cap: Measure where the time goes before tuning, because a setting that speeds up the wrong part changes nothing.

name: p4-0410-privilege-module-table
title: Privilege and module layer symptoms
spec: 1600-wide SVG, rows of Symptom to Fix from the table: Missing sudo password (-K, ansible_become_password, or passwordless sudo); sudo: a terminal is required (remove requiretty, pipelining); python not found (ansible_python_interpreter, raw bootstrap, interpreter_python auto_silent); Failed to set permissions on the temporary files (install acl, pipelining); MODULE FAILURE with traceback (install missing library such as psycopg2 on the target); apt lock or dpkg locked (lock_timeout, wait for unattended-upgrades); Unsupported parameters for module (ansible-doc, align collection version). Orange on the first row.
alt: A table of privilege and module symptoms with the fix for each.
cap: Check privilege first, because it is a more common cause than a module problem.
